result.exception_message: np.linalg.lstsq requires a matrix backend, and DefaultEngine has none installed or the installed one declined these operands. NumSharp.Core is 100 % managed C# and ships no matrix factorisation of its own, so — unlike the matrix products, which always have a managed kernel to fall back to — there is nothing to compute this with. Reference the NumSharp.Interop.OpenBLAS NuGet package — it assigns TensorEngine.Blas an IBlasBackend from a [ModuleInitializer], so adding the package reference is the whole opt-in. The backend serves this operation through its IBlasBackend.TryLstsq.
